svg.aria-label: Fig 5. Planned code lookups. A card catalog cabinet holds five drawers: HCPCS Level II from CMS, ICD-10-CM from CDC/NCHS, CARC values and RARC values with our own labels, and a locked CPT drawer marked not used. An agent asks for the CARC value CO-197 from a synthetic denial. The catalog answers with the value and our own label, prior_auth. A catalog check confirms each code is in the catalog and matches its format, and rejects CPT. Planned, not built.

An agent asks for the CARC value CO-197 from a synthetic denial. The catalog answers with the value and our own label, prior_auth. svg.text: Code values only. No CPT. Planned design, not built.
agents pick codes from the catalog only
1 The catalog holds small public subsets: HCPCS Level II (CMS) and ICD-10-CM (CDC/NCHS),
with attribution. CARC and RARC hold code values with our own labels, not X12 text.
2 The CPT drawer stays locked. We use no CPT codes or descriptors, and no AMA license (D-009).
3 An agent asks for a code value. Example: CO-197, a CARC value on a synthetic denial.
4 The catalog returns the value and our own category label (example: prior_auth).
5 A check confirms that every code is in the catalog and matches its format.
No free-text codes go into a claim, a prompt or a letter.
